title: Observational Indistinguishability and Integrity Blind Regions in Hybrid Quantum-Classical Workflows
description: Version 1.3.3 reproducibility artifact of Paper 1.5. This is a bibliographic/editorial correction only: no experiment, kernel, draw, model, seed, intervention, policy decision or scientific evidence was rerun or changed. The experimental evidence remains frozen at version 1.3.0 (DOI 10.5281/zenodo.22648573), and the methodology is unchanged from 1.3.2. Following a cutoff-complete literature audit (2026-09-08), the manuscript adds verified prior art on adaptive drift evasion, dependence-aware conformal multiple testing, quantum provenance, Simplex runtime assurance, security-ML evaluation bias and RATS attestation; upgrades published metadata for the quantum-security primer, QEMI and quantum Design by Contract; corrects Quantum Leak and Qiskit metadata; and sharpens positioning against VAMP, QCIVET and QML-PipeGuard. The central contribution remains claim-relative minimum evidence granularity in a workflow-wide information-set lattice: a trusted same-batch aggregate can certify conclusion or aggregate integrity, item-identity integrity requires item-aligned trusted evidence, and some trust root outside the declared adversarial rewrite class is unavoidable. Contents include code, tests, eight SHA-256 evidence manifests, compact derived evidence, figures, formal core, amendment audit, adversary model, manuscript sources and submission PDFs.
